title: Extreme input lag caused by PowerToys running in the background

judgment.rationale: The original report gives a fullscreen-game trigger and delayed keyboard input, while the latest author says their case is fixed and other commenters may still be affected. No current affected reporter identifies a PowerToys module or version, so a broad hook hypothesis must be tested before a code fix.
evidence: The original report describes 1–5 second keyboard and gameplay input delays after launching a fullscreen game with PowerToys running.
The latest reporter says their case was fixed by a later update, while noting that other commenters still report similar symptoms.
The issue body gives a concrete fullscreen-game trigger; the latest comment explicitly says the original author is fixed but others may remain affected.

Keyboard Manager uses a low-level keyboard hook and forwards events into remapping. Source at pinned main (237dc893c8c76b1bfa65994afda41ea7315a914c): https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/237dc893c8c76b1bfa65994afda41ea7315a914c/src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEngineLibrary/KeyboardManager.cpp

Grab And Move also uses a low-level mouse hook; distinct input-hook modules must be isolated rather than assumed to share one defect. Source at pinned main (237dc893c8c76b1bfa65994afda41ea7315a914c): https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/237dc893c8c76b1bfa65994afda41ea7315a914c/src/modules/GrabAndMove/GrabAndMove/main.cpp

fix_assessment.rationale: This remains an applicable input-latency report, but the suspected hook/module is uncertain; a targeted reporter comparison is needed before selecting an implementation.

proposed_fixes.title: Attribute fullscreen input lag to a specific PowerToys hook
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: a PowerToys global input hook or a module interaction can delay input during fullscreen workloads; the available discussion does not identify which module, or establish that the currently affected reports share one cause.
plan: Ask a currently affected commenter for the current PowerToys version, fullscreen application, and whether lag persists with PowerToys exited.
In a controlled maintainer run, isolate the responsible module by comparing no PowerToys, all modules disabled, and one input-hook module at a time.
Only change the module/path that reproduces the delay; add a fullscreen input-latency regression for the confirmed trigger.
verification: The identified current scenario has no 1–5 second input delay with the responsible module fixed.
Unrelated modules retain normal behavior and do not inherit an unsupported shared-root assumption.
